text:
incident-bot: ALERT — GPU pool eu-west-1-gpu-3 at 95% queue depth, autoscaler failing to add nodes (scale_limit_reached). triggering pager.
oncall-sre: Paging in. Looking at queue metrics now.
Maya (SRE): I see sustained enqueue rate spike from tenant `playground-demo` since 03:04 UTC. Queue growth started ~5m ago. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing with "quota_exceeded" from cloud provider.
Tariq (Runtime): Runtime shows backlog spilling into short-lived overflow queue. Some requests are marked low-priority; we can start shedding those if needed. Also can enable fallback to quantized model variant to reduce GPU footprint.
Liz (Eng-Platform): Opening infra console — confirmed quota error: account limit for GPUs in region hit. No recent infra changes from our side. Provider console shows pending provisioning requests throttled by quota.
Sam (Support): Heads up — we have 2 customers reporting elevated latency on embeddings endpoints. I flagged them; CS is gathering customer impact details.
Anna (Product): ETA-sensitive service is affected for some customers; let's try minimal customer impact strategy first (throttle non-critical workloads, enable soft-fallback) before any broad evictions.
Maya (SRE): Agreed. Plan A: 1) Abort non-essential batches 2) Enable fallback quantized model for `default` route 3) Apply temporary tenant-level rate-limits for noisy tenants 4) Request emergency quota bump from cloud provider.
Tariq (Runtime): I can flip fallback model routing via feature flag: `runtime.fallback.quantize=true` for eu-west-1. That will reduce average GPU memory usage by ~40% per worker.
Liz (Eng-Platform): I'll open a provider support case and request emergency quota increase + check spare capacity in adjacent region (eu-west-2). Also checking reserved capacity pools for potential warm nodes.
ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=pool=eu-west-1-gpu-3 -o wide`
Results: 42 pods Running, 3 Pending (OOM?), 0 Succeeded.
Maya (SRE): Rolling the fallback now. Tariq, please apply the flag. I'll start rate-limiting noisy tenants. Sam, can you map which customer requests are high volume so we can target limits?
Tariq (Runtime): Applying flag now.
Tariq (Runtime): Done. Streaming logs show progressive eviction of large KV caches and model swap to q4_0 quantized variant.
oncall-sre: Noted CPU and memory on nodes dropped ~30% within 90s. Queue head latency reduced from 3.4s -> 1.2s for most routes.
Sam (Support): I pushed a note to the two affected customers: "We're actively mitigating a capacity event; you may experience reduced throughput for a short period. We'll follow up once stabilized." Customers acknowledged.
Liz (Eng-Platform): Provider replied to support case: "We can expedite quota bump in 15-20m if you approve." Also found 6 GPUs idle in eu-west-2 reserved pool; cross-region routing is possible but will add ~60ms latency.
Anna (Product): Do not route cross-region unless we confirm customers impacted will benefit. Prioritize in-region mitigations first.
Maya (SRE): Temporary tenant throttles are live for top 3 noisy tenants (playground-demo, loadtest-inc, ci-spot). Queues now stable, but autoscaler still reporting repeat failures when trying to create new nodes — provider rate limits on creation calls.
Tariq (Runtime): We should enable admission control to prefer small-request batching and reduce new worker spinups. I'll flip `admission.batch.size` down for eu-west-1.
Maya (SRE): Doing it.
ops-bot: Command executed: `curl -X POST "https://internal-admin/api/tenants/throttle" -d '{"tenants":["playground-demo","loadtest-inc","ci-spot"],"rate":0.3}'`
oncall-sre: After throttles and fallback quantized model: tail latency is down, overall throughput at ~70% of normal but stable. No further pagers in the last 4m.
Liz (Eng-Platform): Provider confirmed quota bump approved. ETA for additional GPUs provisioning: ~18m. I'll coordinate warm-up.
Sam (Support): Customer A confirms latency improved, Customer B still sees occasional failures at peak. Sending more details to Maya.
Maya (SRE): Investigating failures — looks like some long-running jobs pinned GPUs and weren't classified as low-priority. Initiating eviction for idle sessions older than 10m.
Tariq (Runtime): Eviction script:
```
for session in $(query-sessions --region eu-west-1 | jq -r '.sessions[] | select(.idle_seconds > 600) | .id'); do
  kill-session $session || echo "fail $session"
done
```
Maya (SRE): Evictions freed 4 GPUs' worth; queue stabilized further. Autoscaler now able to provision new nodes and add 8 GPUs, starting to come online.
ops-bot: Provider events: new instances are initializing, health checks pending.
oncall-sre: Bridge not needed at this point; keep channel for live ops. If autoscaler errors repeat, we'll escalate to a bridge.
Anna (Product): Actionable customer-visible note: we'll publish a short status update once fully recovered. Sam, coordinate wording.
Sam (Support): Will draft and post a status note after Liz confirms new capacity is healthy.
Liz (Eng-Platform): New GPUs passed health checks. Capacity surplus + autoscaler errors cleared. Reverting temporary throttles and fallback in 5m if stable.
Tariq (Runtime): Reverting `runtime.fallback.quantize=false` in 30s.
Tariq (Runtime): Done. Running canary requests — latency and correctness checks pass.
Maya (SRE): Reverting tenant throttles now.
ops-bot: Command executed: `curl -X POST "https://internal-admin/api/tenants/unthrottle" -d '{"tenants":["playground-demo","loadtest-inc","ci-spot"]}'`
oncall-sre: No more queue growth. System returned to normal baselines. Closing pager in 10m unless new alerts.
Sam (Support): Posted interim status update: "We mitigated a capacity event by enabling temporary model fallbacks and targeted throttling. Additional capacity has been provisioned; we're monitoring for 30m." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/6054321987
Maya (SRE): Postmortem notes (initial):
- Summary: Autoscaler failed to provision due to cloud quota exhaustion causing queue growth and elevated latency for some customers. Rapid mitigations (quantized fallback, tenant throttles, eviction) prevented large-scale customer impact.
- Root cause: cloud account GPU quota insufficient for burst spikes + provider creation rate limits that triggered repeated scale attempt failures.
- Contributing factors: noisy long-running interactive sessions not correctly classified as preemptible; lack of emergency quota playbook with provider contact details.
- Impact: Two customers reported latency spikes and transient failures; overall service latency increased for ~22 minutes. No data loss.
- Timeline: 03:04 alert -> 03:06 fallback & throttles -> 03:10 eviction -> 03:28 new capacity healthy -> 03:35 services normalized.
- Action items:
  1) Short term (P0, owner: Liz): Document provider emergency quota process + automate case creation with priority template. ETA 3d.
  2) Medium (P1, owner: Tariq): Add a runtime auto-fallback policy that can be enabled per-region automatically when autoscaler errors exceed threshold. ETA 2w.
  3) Medium (P1, owner: Maya): Improve session classifier to mark interactive long-running sessions as preemptible or cap max runtime by default. ETA 1w.
  4) Long term (P2, owner: Platform): Increase buffer reserved GPUs in eu-west-1 or enable warm standby across regions with automatic cross-region routing rules. ETA 1mo.
  5) Process (P1, owner: Ops): Add provider creation rate limit detection to autoscaler health checks and stop cyclic scale attempts when provider returns 429/RateLimit.
Maya (SRE): I'll start the postmortem doc and assign actions in the tracker. Please add any missing items.
Anna (Product): Add a customer communication follow-up: personalized outreach to affected customers and credit consideration if SLA impacted.
Sam (Support): Noted. Will coordinate with CS.
Liz (Eng-Platform): I'll own P0 and follow up with cloud account team.
oncall-sre: Closing note: great triage and calm coordination. The mix of runtime mitigations + infra follow-up prevented broader outage. Marking incident as "mitigated".
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED — 6054321987 (mitigated).
